title: Risk-weighted intake pipeline for security & compliance requests
creator: Avery Patel
description: Goal: Build an automated intake pipeline that classifies and prioritizes inbound security & compliance requests (SOC2/ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) and routes them to the right team and SLA lane. Scope: inbound customer asks submitted via support forms, sales intake, and Customer Success. The pipeline should produce a deterministic risk score, suggested evidence bundles, recommended assignee queue (security, legal, solutions), and required SLA target. Out of scope: full questionnaire automation and legal clause negotiation. Approach: 1) Map common questionnaire types to a canonical taxonomy (framework: SOC2, ISO27001 sections, HIPAA categories, GDPR data residency/processing, DPA clauses), 2) Design a lightweight rule + ML hybrid scorer that ingests metadata (customer tier, region, requested evidence, data residency constraints, ask complexity) and produces a risk/effort score, 3) Wire scorer to routing rules that map score bands to SLA lanes and escalation paths, 4) Precompute evidence bundles based on catalog (SSO screenshots, SOC2 cert, encryption docs, data flow diagram), 5) Add observability to measure triage accuracy and cycle time. Success metrics: median triage time <= 8 hours for P1 asks, routing accuracy >= 85% (manual overrides measured), reduction in manual MRR-support handoffs by 40% in pilot accounts. Trade-offs considered: pure ML may be brittle on rare asks; we will start with deterministic rules and augment with a logistic model trained on historical triage decisions. Privacy: pipeline must not store customer questionnaire attachments in plaintext; all artifacts referenced by S3 links with access controls. Compliance: design must include audit logs for every routing decision for future SOC2 evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical taxonomy documented and reviewed by Security and Legal
Prototype scorer returns a risk_score and effort_estimate for a sample of 200 historical requests with >= 80% match to historical routing
Routing table maps score bands to at least three SLA lanes and corresponding owner queues
Evidence bundle mapping created for top 10 common ask templates (PDFs/SSO/SOC2/diagrams)
Instrumented metrics dashboard tracking triage latency, manual overrides, and false routing rate
Playbook for manual escalation and override recorded in Confluence
comments: 2026-03-01 — Avery Patel: Kickoff with Security, Legal, CS. Collected sample set of 412 past questionnaire asks from Zendesk and internal intake forms. Agreed to prioritize SOC2/ISO and DPAs for the first phase.

2026-03-03 — Marisol Chen: Draft taxonomy v0 shared (Confluence). Security requested explicit fields for data residency and encryption-at-rest. Legal asked for a DPA clause index to map ask->contract clause quickly.

2026-03-05 — Eng triage (Luis Gomez): Recommended hybrid rule+model approach. We can start with rule engine for high-confidence patterns and add a lightweight classifier for ambiguous cases. Flag: need training labels from historical routing decisions.

2026-03-06 — CS feedback (Priya Singh): Proposed SLA lanes: fast-track (24h), standard (5 business days), deferred (10+ business days). Suggested pilot with top 12 enterprise customers to validate accuracy.

2026-03-08 — Security review (Tomas Novak): Must ensure all routing decisions are logged with user id, timestamp, input hash. Also requested encryption key rotation notes be attached to evidence bundles. Assigned follow-up to ENG-5912 for logging plumbing.
